description:
EcoNex es un grupo orientado a conectar la tecnología, la innovación y el cuidado del medio ambiente para desarrollar ideas y soluciones que contribuyan a un futuro más sostenible.

El nombre combina Eco, que representa la ecología y el compromiso ambiental, con Nex, inspirado en la palabra nexus, que significa conexión. Juntos simbolizan la unión entre las personas, la tecnología y el planeta.
summary:
El desafío que decidimos afrontar es la implementación de tecnología en granjas agrícolas para mejorar la planificación de la rotación de cultivos y el manejo sostenible del suelo.
Nuestro proyecto consiste en desarrollar una página web que integre información geográfica, meteorológica y climática de una parcela, datos de regiones fitogeográficas y datos obtenidos mediante imágenes satelitales proporcionadas por la NASA. Además, permitirá incorporar información del suelo, como PH, conductividad eléctrica (CE) y porcentaje de sodificación.
A partir de estos datos, la plataforma orientará al productor sobre los cultivos más adecuados y diseñará sistemas de rotación, incluyendo cultivos de descanso. Estos contribuirán a conservar el suelo, aportar materia orgánica, reducir el agotamiento de nutrientes y ayudar a regular la salinidad, el pH y la sodificación.
La aplicación podrá vincularse con estaciones meteorológicas locales mediante bluetooth y wifi con un microcontrolador ESP32 y sensores (termistores NTC o DS18B20) para monitorear temperatura, precipitaciones e intensidad de luz solar. Esto permitirá generar alertas tempranas ante cambios ambientales y facilitar decisiones productivas.
El objetivo es brindar una herramienta tecnológica que permita maximizar el rendimiento, reducir pérdidas y promover buenas prácticas agrícolas y el uso sostenible de los recursos.
details:
AgroAlerta: Intelligent Platform for Agroclimatic Analysis, Land Management, and Agricultural Planning

1. What Is AgroAlerta?

AgroAlerta is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform that integrates meteorological, geographical, and soil-related information with artificial intelligence to help farmers manage their land, identify climate risks, and evaluate crop production alternatives.

The project was developed in response to the need for accessible technological tools that allow agricultural producers to analyze environmental conditions before making important decisions regarding planting, crop rotation, and soil management.

The platform is initially focused on agricultural producers in Argentina, particularly in Santiago del Estero, although it includes geographical features that allow users to explore other regions.

Its main objective is to transform climatic and agricultural data into understandable, practical information that supports risk prevention and sustainable agricultural planning.

2. How Does AgroAlerta Work?

The system consists of several interconnected modules that provide different agricultural analysis and management tools.

A. Agricultural Land Selection and Management

Farmers can locate their agricultural land through an interactive map using geographical coordinates, including latitude and longitude.

The platform allows users to:

  • Search for provinces, cities, and geographical locations.
  • View standard street maps and satellite imagery.
  • Manually draw field boundaries using polygons.
  • Automatically calculate the approximate area of a selected field in hectares.
  • Identify the province, country, region, subregion, geographical coordinates, and estimated altitude.
  • Customize field boundary colors.
  • Save, retrieve, and modify agricultural parcel information.

The information is stored in a SQL Server database for future consultations and integration with other system modules.

B. Climate Monitoring and Agroclimatic Analysis

AgroAlerta connects to external meteorological services to obtain environmental information associated with the selected location.

The main variables analyzed include:

  • Maximum and minimum temperatures.
  • Rainfall and precipitation.
  • Relative humidity.
  • Wind speed.
  • Current weather conditions.
  • Historical climate patterns.

Farmers can select specific date ranges using interactive calendars and visualize the information through comparative charts.

The platform distinguishes between historical observations, available weather forecasts, and long-term climatological trends.

C. Agroclimatic Risk Prevention

The system performs preliminary assessments to identify weather conditions that could negatively affect agricultural production.

It considers potential risks such as prolonged periods of low rainfall, intense precipitation, and extreme temperatures, depending on the available indicators.

The results help farmers understand the level of potential risk and identify environmental conditions that may affect their fields.

These evaluations are intended to support preventive decision-making and do not replace official weather alerts or specialized assessments.

D. Soil Analysis and Agricultural Suitability

One of the platform's central features is the evaluation of soil characteristics.

Farmers can manually enter laboratory soil analysis results, including:

  • pH: the soil's acidity or alkalinity level.
  • Exchangeable Sodium Percentage (ESP): an indicator of soil sodicity.
  • Electrical Conductivity (ECe): an indicator of soil salinity, expressed in dS/m.

AgroAlerta compares these values with general agronomic reference ranges and thresholds for different crops.

The platform generates comparison tables displaying the recorded values, reference parameters, and potential limitations.

It also provides soil management suggestions and indicates when professional advice from an agricultural engineer or additional laboratory testing may be necessary.

E. Regional Crop Recommendations

The platform considers crops commonly grown in different agricultural regions of Argentina, including Northwestern Argentina (NOA), Northeastern Argentina (NEA), the Pampas, Cuyo, and Patagonia.

The crops analyzed include wheat, soybeans, corn, sorghum, sunflower, cotton, barley, alfalfa, beans, and other regional agricultural products.

AgroAlerta combines geographical information, available climatic conditions, and soil characteristics to identify potentially suitable crop alternatives.

These recommendations are preliminary and must be complemented with additional information, including soil moisture, fertility, soil depth, water availability, and local agricultural management practices.

F. Crop Rotation Planning

The system includes a crop rotation module that allows farmers to identify the crop previously planted in a field and evaluate possible alternatives for the next growing season.

Farmers can select two main objectives:

1. Maximize soil fertility and promote nutrient replenishment.

The platform evaluates potential crop rotation alternatives based on crop characteristics, plant diversity, and nutritional requirements.

2. Diversify agricultural income and reduce production risks.

The system proposes crop alternatives that may help diversify production and reduce dependence on a single crop.

For each recommendation, AgroAlerta provides an explanation of the suggested crop, its potential benefits, associated risks, and additional agronomic factors that should be evaluated before planting.

G. AgroBot: Artificial Intelligence Assistant

AgroAlerta incorporates AgroBot, a virtual assistant designed to answer agricultural questions.

The chatbot uses language models through the Groq API, an artificial intelligence inference platform.

AgroBot is designed to respond to questions about:

  • Agricultural crops and crop rotation.
  • Soil properties and management.
  • Climate risks.
  • Droughts and precipitation.
  • Interpretation of agricultural information.
  • General farming recommendations.

Its integration can include contextual information from registered fields and agricultural alerts, enabling responses related to the farmer's specific working environment.

Artificial intelligence complements the platform's analytical capabilities but does not replace professional agronomic expertise.

H. Weather Station Integration

The project also includes a module designed to register and configure connections with weather stations.

Its purpose is to support future integration of local meteorological measurements from compatible devices.

Actual integration depends on the communication protocols and technical capabilities of each weather station.

3. What Are the Benefits of AgroAlerta?

The main benefits include:

1. Improved decision-making: helps farmers interpret climate, geographical, and soil information within a single platform.

2. Agricultural risk prevention: supports early identification of potentially unfavorable environmental conditions.

3. Better crop planning: allows farmers to evaluate agricultural alternatives according to field characteristics.

4. Responsible soil management: encourages the analysis of soil acidity, salinity, sodicity, and crop rotation.

5. Technological accessibility: provides agricultural analysis tools through a web interface accessible from computers and mobile devices.

6. Centralized agricultural information: combines maps, fields, meteorological data, soil analysis, and artificial intelligence in one platform.

7. Agricultural knowledge support: provides clear explanations to help users understand technical information and interpret results.

4. What Is the Expected Impact of the Project?

AgroAlerta aims to contribute to the digital transformation of agriculture, particularly among small and medium-sized farmers who need affordable and accessible planning and analysis tools.

Its expected impact can be divided into three main areas.

Agricultural and Economic Impact

The platform aims to improve access to information for selecting crops, planning planting periods, and anticipating adverse weather conditions.

Better-informed decisions may help farmers reduce avoidable losses and improve agricultural planning.

Environmental Impact

AgroAlerta promotes responsible soil management by encouraging crop rotation and helping identify limitations related to salinity, sodicity, and soil degradation.

The project aims to contribute to more sustainable agricultural practices and better preservation of natural resources.

Technological and Social Impact

The platform seeks to make digital technologies, geographical information, and artificial intelligence more accessible to agricultural producers who may have limited access to specialized technological solutions.

In the long term, AgroAlerta aims to evolve into a comprehensive digital agriculture platform combining public environmental information, local measurements, and agronomic analysis.

5. Development Tools, Programming Languages, and Technologies

Programming and Web Development

C# and ASP.NET Core 8: form the technological foundation of the web server, business logic, and database communication.

Razor Pages and HTML5: are used to build the application's interfaces and organize its pages.

CSS3: provides modern, responsive visual design with customizable appearance options.

JavaScript: enables interactive features, API requests, map interactions, charts, and user interface controls.

JSON and HTTP services: facilitate communication between the application and external data providers.

Database Technologies

Microsoft SQL Server: stores agricultural field information, geographical coordinates, field areas, polygon boundaries, and other application records.

SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS): is used to administer the database, execute queries, and maintain its structure.

Microsoft.Data.SqlClient: enables database communication between the C# application and SQL Server.

Software Development Tools

  • Microsoft Visual Studio: the primary development environment for programming, compilation, and debugging.
  • Git: a version control system used to manage changes to the source code.
  • GitHub: a platform for hosting and managing the project's source code.
  • NuGet: used for managing project dependencies.
  • Web browsers: used for application execution and user interface testing.

APIs and External Services

Open-Meteo API: provides weather information, available forecasts, and historical meteorological data for agricultural analysis and chart visualization.

NASA POWER: an environmental and climatological data source considered during project development for historical weather information and climate trend analysis.

Mapping and Geographical Services: support interactive maps, satellite imagery, geographical searches, coordinate identification, regional classification, and agricultural field boundary visualization.

Groq API: provides access to artificial intelligence language models used by AgroBot.

OpenAI API: was used during an earlier development stage of the AI assistant, before exploring Groq as a lower-cost alternative.

Artificial Intelligence Technologies

AgroBot's main AI integration uses Groq, with a language model from the GPT-OSS family configured to answer agriculture-related questions.

Artificial intelligence is used to:

  • Facilitate interactions with the platform.
  • Explain agricultural information.
  • Provide contextual guidance.
  • Help users interpret climate and soil conditions.
  • Answer general agricultural questions.

AI does not independently determine crop suitability. Soil comparisons and agricultural recommendations must remain supported by documented agronomic criteria.

Hardware Requirements

The application was developed using personal computers running the Windows operating system and standard software development tools.

Farmers can access the platform using a computer, smartphone, or tablet with an internet connection and a compatible web browser.

The system also considers future integration with physical weather stations equipped with sensors that measure temperature, humidity, and precipitation.

However, owning a personal weather station is not a mandatory requirement for using AgroAlerta.

6. What Makes AgroAlerta Innovative and Creative?

AgroAlerta's main innovation is its ability to integrate different sources of agricultural and environmental information into a single interactive decision-support platform.

Unlike applications that simply display weather forecasts, AgroAlerta aims to relate environmental conditions to the characteristics of individual agricultural fields and the requirements of different crops.

Farmers can draw their field boundaries, consult meteorological information, enter laboratory soil results, evaluate crop alternatives, and communicate with an AI assistant within the same digital environment.

Another innovative feature is the comparison between actual soil measurements entered by users and general agronomic reference parameters.

This allows the platform to explain potential soil limitations and suggest which additional information may be necessary to make better agricultural decisions.

Its modular architecture also makes it possible to incorporate additional crops, meteorological stations, environmental indicators, and analytical models in future versions.

The project combines software development, geographical information systems, environmental data, agricultural knowledge, and artificial intelligence to create a practical technological tool.

7. What Factors Were Considered During Development?

Several factors were considered throughout the design and development of AgroAlerta.

Accessibility and usability: creating an intuitive interface that can be used by people with different levels of technological knowledge.

Regional agricultural conditions: incorporating crops representative of Argentina's different agricultural regions.

Data quality and reliability: distinguishing between measured observations, historical climate information, meteorological estimates, and weather forecasts.

Agricultural sustainability: supporting responsible soil management, water conservation, and crop diversification.

Scientific limitations: avoiding definitive agricultural recommendations when essential information is unavailable.

Development and operational costs: prioritizing accessible technologies, publicly available environmental data, and artificial intelligence services with free usage tiers.

Scalability: designing a platform capable of incorporating additional features and expanding geographically.

Data storage and security: storing agricultural information in a structured database while considering authentication, user permissions, and data protection for future public deployment.

8. Conclusion

AgroAlerta is an innovative technological initiative designed to improve agricultural planning, environmental analysis, and agroclimatic risk prevention.

By integrating web programming, databases, geographical information, meteorological services, and artificial intelligence, the platform aims to transform complex and dispersed data into accessible, practical information for farmers.

The project combines technological innovation, agronomic knowledge, and user-friendly design, with a long-term vision of developing increasingly comprehensive digital agriculture tools.

Its ultimate goal is to help agricultural producers make more informed, responsible, and sustainable decisions regarding soil management, crop selection, and agricultural production planning.
